title: Repipe & Leak Detection
headline:
Find the leak first.
Then fix it once.
shortDescription: Whole-house repipe (galvanized or polybutylene to PEX or copper), slab-leak detection, hidden-leak diagnosis, and targeted repairs that don't tear up half your house.
lead: A lot of older NW Portland homes still have galvanized or original polybutylene supply lines, and most of the leak calls I run are some version of that pipe finally giving up. Before I cut drywall I find the leak — pressure tests, acoustic listening, infrared on suspect walls, and a moisture meter to confirm where it's tracking. Once I know exactly where it is, the repair is small. The houses that get torn apart are usually the ones where someone started cutting before they knew where the leak was.

sections.heading: What this covers
sections.intro: From a single dripping fitting to a full-house repipe — same plumber, same standards.

items.label: Leak detection visit — $189 flat
items.body: Full diagnostic: meter test, pressure isolation, acoustic, moisture mapping, and a written report with photos. Credited toward repair

items.label: Visible leak repair — from $245
items.body: Compression fitting, slip joint, valve, hose bib, or accessible PEX/copper repair. Per-job estimate over 1 hour of work

items.label: Slab leak repair — $1,400–$3,800
items.body: Detection plus repair via reroute (most common, least destructive) or spot repair through the slab. Free written estimate

items.label: Whole-house repipe — $7,500–$14,500
items.body: Galvanized or polybutylene replaced with PEX-A home runs from a manifold. Includes patching open access points; drywall finish coordinated with a trusted partner

items.label: Pressure regulator install — $475 flat
items.body: Many older Westside homes run 90+ PSI from the street. A PRV protects every fixture in the house and usually pays for itself in saved appliance lifespan

items.label: Annual whole-home plumbing inspection — $189
items.body: Visual inspection of supply, drain, fixtures, water heater, shutoffs, and outdoor hose bibs. Written report and a photo of every issue I flag

sections.heading: How a repipe goes
sections.body: Plan the access points, run the new lines, swap one fixture group at a time, pressure-test, then patch.
items: Walkthrough and free written estimate — what's getting replaced, where the access points are, how many days you'll be down to one bathroom
Set up the manifold (usually in the garage or utility room) and run PEX-A home runs through joist bays and wall cavities
Cut over one fixture group at a time so the house stays usable as much as possible — typically one full bathroom out at any given time
Pressure-test the system, sign off with the inspector, and reconnect every fixture with new shutoffs
Photos of every joint and run before drywall closes. 5-year workmanship warranty on the repipe itself, manufacturer warranty pass-through on PEX (typically 25-year)
